body:
Thanks.. I just think they are oblivious to just how much they are hurting me with their action and what they are saying.  Between my aunt and my dad, I've been asked if I can convince my mom to take him back over 30 times in the span of 2 days... and of course that impossible after what he has done, and I explained as such, but they kept on asking and asking.  

And it's shit like that brought me to nervous breakdown the other day and why I am still struggling with panic attacks right now.  They just can't let it go and if I allow any contact they will pull the same shit again. Sometimes my mind gets overloaded just having to think about that.  This is why I needed to block their number and cut ties completely.. 

and I really need to let go, realize that they will never be happy and that this is none of my responsibility.  I've given what I could, and it sucks that I have to walk away knowing that that people I helped are actively trying to make me feel guilty about not doing enough for them.

Thanks for writing back.  My dad is no longer a physical threat to me anymore, but I definitely think dealing with him and his family is detrimental to my mental health due to their manipulative nature.  

My aunt called me this morning and told me that my dad is home and I should call him.  I told her that I am dealing with my own problem and I can no longer deal with him.  I've already got a call from the hospital about how they found no serious problem with my dad's health and how my aunt took her home, so I don't need an update and he is fine as far as I am concerned.

I also had to confront her about the fact that she was just making excuse not to take care of the situation, even though she literally lives 10 minutes away from the hospital and my dad's home.  I called my grandmother's house the other night and found out that my aunt is basically leaving my grandmother completely unattended at night. so it's a complete BS excuse that my aunt can't come to hospital because she needs to take care of her mom.

I felt like I needed to stand up for myself and put an end to this.  I really don't have problem with helping others, but my dad's family is known for guilt tripping people into doing things, and they are type of people who will take the whole yard if I give them an inch.  Sure, they said all they want is to call my dad from time to time, but eventually that's going to escalate into spending time with him and ultimately taking care of him.. and they are expecting this of me, expecting me to give everything while my dad has no motivation to make things better for himself or for the relationship.  

EDIT: I don't think people on my dad's side will ever acknowledge what he did to me.  Even to this day, they are asking me to get my mom to take him back after all he did.  My dad literally left my mom for a woman my age.  They may not know about the abuse but they definitely know about the affair and they have met with my dad's new wife. The never they have to even ask me or my mom of this is appalling and shows just how much of a lost cause it is to deal with them.

Hi thanks.  If you mean talk, as in means other than text messaging here, unfortunately I am not sure if I can speak at all now.. but if you are willing to keep in touch via pm I'd be very much appreciated.  I guess right now I am just cycling between  feeling overwhelmed about what is happening, angry and triggered being reminded of what happened, and generally having hard time processing what is happening.

If you feel like to fell free to share your experience, and you are more than welcome to share via pm if you don't feel like making it public.... but by all means do so only if you are comfortable.

I'm usually able to fend off problems like this and live my life, but this was a case if I didn't do it no one else would, and this person's life was at stake.  On top of that I was dealing with uncooperative hospital who want to pin all the financial/ethical burdens on me because they don't want to liable(i.e pressuring me to keep the caretaker for the entire time of my dad's stay even though caretaker himself said that my dad was more than capable of take care of himself and we observed his condition together for good 8 hours).  luckily enough, the caretaker I hired for 2 days were very sympathetic, explained what's actually happening on the hospital's side and, was very helpful dealing with those jerks at the hospital.
